checks.title: GitHub Actions security audit (zizmor)
checks.why: Runs zizmor over the workflows GitHub executes (template injection, dangerous triggers, credential persistence, cache poisoning, excessive permissions). CI holds release and signing secrets, so a workflow flaw is a supply-chain compromise. Deduction per finding by severity x confidence, capped at 3 points per audit.

checks.title: Third-party actions pinned to commit SHAs
checks.why: A tag like @v4 can be moved by whoever controls the action (tj-actions/changed-files, 2025). Score is the share of external `uses:` references pinned to a 40-character SHA (or image digest).

checks.title: Least-privilege GITHUB_TOKEN
checks.why: Workflows without an explicit `permissions:` block inherit the repository default, which can be read-write on everything. Score is the share of workflows that scope the token; write-all is penalised, risky triggers are reported.

checks.title: LLM agents in CI resist prompt injection
checks.why: Workflows that run coding agents (codex-action, claude-code-action, gemini-cli, ...) on issues, comments or PRs read attacker-written text. Interpolating that text into the prompt, letting any user trigger the agent, or giving the run write scopes turns the agent into a confused deputy. zizmor does not model this. Null if no agent workflows.

findings.message: Runs an LLM agent (openai/codex-action) on untrusted trigger(s): issues; treat everything it reads as hostile input.
`allow-users: "*"` lets any GitHub user trigger the agent.
`allow-users: "*"` lets any GitHub user trigger the agent.
Agent output feeds a workflow holding write scopes (issues); a steered agent can make it label, comment or push.
Mitigation present: the agent runs read-only / without sudo.

checks.title: Rust unsafe code is justified
checks.why: Memory-safety bugs live in `unsafe`. Each unsafe block/fn/impl should carry a `// SAFETY:` comment stating the invariant it relies on (clippy::undocumented_unsafe_blocks). Score is the documented share.

findings.message: 548 unsafe sites in 73 files across 122 Cargo manifests; 47 carry a SAFETY justification; 0 crate roots forbid unsafe_code; clippy::undocumented_unsafe_blocks not enabled.

checks.title: Container images hardened
checks.why: Dockerfiles should pin base images by digest, drop root, avoid ADD from URLs and keep secrets out of layers.

findings.message: Base image 'ubuntu:24.04' is not pinned by digest; rebuilds can pull a different (possibly compromised) image.
Base image 'mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/base:ubuntu-24.04' is not pinned by digest; rebuilds can pull a different (possibly compromised) image.

checks.title: Signed, attested releases
checks.why: Release workflows should attest build provenance, sign artifacts, publish with OIDC instead of long-lived tokens and ship checksums, so users can verify what they install.

findings.message: Missing build provenance attestation (SLSA / actions/attest); consumers cannot verify where artifacts came from.
Has OIDC trusted publishing / short-lived credentials ('id-token: write').
